name: Precinct 2008
tagline: A field guide and poll worker roster for one precinct's election inspector, all stored on the iPhone and working without a signal.
about:
Precinct 2008 is a reference app for the inspector of one polling place. It holds a bundled 226-page poll worker guide that you can search, checklists, a list of key facts, a schedule, and a roster where the inspector keeps their poll workers' names, phone numbers, tags and notes. Everything is built into the app or saved on the phone, so it works in airplane mode.

The app is not a voting tool. It handles no voter information and gives no voting or legal advice. It only shows the guide and the checklists it contains and keeps the inspector's own notes.

collects.where: On your device, in one file that iOS keeps locked while the phone is locked
collects.shared: Nobody. The app has no server and sends nothing. It leaves the phone only through the actions listed in this table.
collects.why: This is the inspector's contact list for their poll workers.

collects.what: Notes about each person. The app also adds short notes itself, such as Called.
collects.where: On your device, in the same file
collects.why: To keep a record of who was contacted and what was said.

collects.what: Schedule items, checklist ticks and a few app settings (for example, that you have seen the welcome screen)
collects.where: On your device, in the same file
collects.why: So the schedule and checklists are as you left them.

collects.what: Backups of all of the above. One is saved about once a day, and one before every import or restore. The newest 30 are kept on the phone.
collects.where: On your device. If you choose a backup folder, a copy is also saved there. The app keeps only the newest 30 of its own backup files in that folder and deletes older ones with the same file name pattern. Copies in that folder are not covered by the phone's file lock.
collects.shared: Nobody, unless you choose a folder that is synced online. In that case the company that runs the folder (for example iCloud Drive or Google Drive) keeps the copy in your account. The app itself does not upload it.

usage_data:
Precinct 2008 keeps a diagnostic log on your phone, in the app's own storage. It writes a line every 10 seconds while the app is running. Each line says whether the app is in the foreground or background, which screen is open, how many people are on the roster, how many checklist items are ticked, the memory in use, the battery level, the free storage space, and whether the last save failed. It also records app opening and closing, tab and screen changes, filter and tag taps, checklist ticks, which guide page you opened, and counts for backups, imports, exports and erasing.

The log is designed not to contain names, phone numbers, notes or what you type. Text is kept only for a short list of fixed labels used by the app itself, and every other piece of text is reduced to its length. Searches and questions are logged only as a count of results and a count of words. The app does not log scrolling, pointer movement or typed text.

The log is not uploaded. The app has no code that sends anything over the internet. Apart from an iPhone, iCloud or computer backup of the phone, the log leaves the phone only if the developer exports it from the app. Log files older than 30 days are deleted when the app opens, and erasing the app's data removes the existing log files (the app then starts a new log that holds only counts). A short line about the system activity, the type of event only, also goes to Apple's system log on the phone.
not_collected: No analytics or crash-reporting tools from other companies, and no other third-party code
No internet connection: the app contains no code to send or receive data
No access to your contacts, camera, microphone, photos or location
No automatic upload of the roster, notes or logs

third_parties.who: The company that runs a backup folder you choose (for example iCloud Drive or Google Drive)
third_parties.what: A full copy of your roster and notes, only if you pick a synced folder as a place for extra backup copies. Pick a folder that only you can open.

Provides TestFlight and the iPhone's own services. If you have iPhone backups turned on, Apple's or your computer's backup of the phone includes the app's saved files, because the app does not exclude them. The app sends no data to Apple itself.

permissions.name: Face ID or passcode (optional)
permissions.why: Only if you turn on Settings, Lock with Face ID or passcode. The app then asks the phone to confirm it is you at launch and each time you return to the app, and hides its screen in the app switcher. The app uses the phone's own Face ID or passcode check and keeps only the on/off switch; it never sees your face or passcode.

permissions.name: Files and folders you pick
permissions.why: The app asks for no other permissions. When you choose a file to import or a folder for backup copies, iOS shows its own file picker, which gives the app access only to what you pick.

retention:
Your roster, notes, schedule changes and checklist ticks stay on the phone until you remove them. Removing a person from the roster deletes that person and their notes from the phone. You get 8 seconds to undo it, and the undo is kept in memory only. Backups made before the removal still contain that person until those backups are deleted; the newest 30 are kept, and Erase All Data deletes all backups saved on the phone. The newest 30 backups are kept on the phone, and you can delete any one of them by swiping on it in Settings. Log files are deleted after 30 days.

To delete everything the app holds, open Settings, then Erase All Data on This iPhone, and confirm. This deletes the roster, notes, checklist ticks and schedule changes, the backups saved on the phone, the existing log files, the app's settings and the temporary export files. The welcome screen then shows again, as on a new install.

Erasing does not touch the backup folder you picked, files you exported and shared, or iPhone backups made by iCloud or your computer. Delete those yourself. Deleting the app from the phone also removes its data on the phone, but not those copies.
children: Precinct 2008 is not made for children. It has no accounts, no ads and no tracking, and it does not send information about anyone to the developer. The roster is whatever the inspector types or imports. If it includes younger poll workers, such as the Student Clerk role, their details stay on the phone in the same way as everyone else's.
support_what:
Precinct 2008 is a field guide for the inspector of one polling place. It puts the county's 226-page poll worker guide on the phone, split into its nine booklets and searchable, along with checklists that link to the guide's pages, a list of key facts, a schedule and a roster of the inspector's poll workers.

It works without a signal. Everything you enter stays on the phone unless you export it or choose a backup folder.
support_steps: Install the app from TestFlight and tap Get started on the welcome screen.
To bring in a roster file, put the file on the phone (for example with AirDrop), then open Settings, then Your data, then Import a Precinct 2008 file, and pick it.
Read the preview that shows what will change. If it looks right, tap Save a safety copy, then replace what's on this iPhone. If not, tap Cancel.
Add people one at a time with the plus button on the People tab. Tap a person to call, text or copy their number, set tags and add notes.
Use the Checklists tab to tick items off, and tap a page number to open that page of the guide.
In Settings, under Automatic backups, tap Back up now, and optionally choose a folder for extra copies.

support_faq.q: Does the app need a signal or internet?
support_faq.a: No. The guide, its text, the checklists and the roster all work in airplane mode. The app has no code that connects to the internet.

On this iPhone, in a file that iOS keeps locked while the phone is locked. You can also turn on an app lock in Settings (Lock with Face ID or passcode; it is off until you turn it on). It goes elsewhere only if you export it, share it or choose a backup folder in Settings.

support_faq.q: How do I back up my roster, and how do I restore it?
support_faq.a: The app saves a backup on the phone about once a day and before every import or restore, and keeps the newest 30. Settings, then Automatic backups, shows them. Tap Restore next to one to see a preview before anything changes. You can also tap Back up now, or choose a folder such as one in iCloud Drive or Google Drive to get extra copies. Those copies contain names and phone numbers, so choose a folder only you can open.

support_faq.q: How do I move my roster to another iPhone or into a spreadsheet?
support_faq.a: Open Settings, then Your data, and tap Prepare export files. You get a full export that opens in this app, plus spreadsheet files for people, the schedule and checklists. They contain names and phone numbers, so share them only with people who should have them. The temporary copies are removed when you leave Settings.

support_faq.q: What does Ask the guide do?
support_faq.a: Type a question on the Guide tab. The app finds the matching pages in the guide. On an iPhone with Apple Intelligence it also writes a short answer from those pages, using Apple's on-device model, and names the pages. On other phones it shows the matching pages.

support_faq.q: The app says it can't open my saved data. What do I do?
support_faq.a: This can happen right after the phone restarts, before it is unlocked. Unlock the phone and tap Try again. If it still fails, you can restore the newest backup. The app keeps the unreadable file as a safety copy first.
Open Settings and choose Erase All Data on This iPhone. It lists what is erased and what is not, then asks you to confirm. It does not touch a backup folder you picked or files you already shared.

Yes. In Settings, turn on Lock with Face ID or passcode. It is off by default. When it is on, the app asks you to unlock it when it opens and each time you come back to it, and its picture in the app switcher is blank. The lock uses the phone's own Face ID or passcode.
